description: Single source of the cited lumbar coupling data for the opt-in segmental lumbar chain (OpenSim_Models #464, #473). Per-level values are listed caudal first in the 'levels' order; Python loads them through lumbar_coupling_data.load_lumbar_coupling_laws. The section is shaped so it can move unchanged into the shared biomech parity standard if the Repository_Management board accepts proposal #2116.

laws.citation: Xu F, Zhou S, Li Z, Jiang S, Chen Z, Sun Z, Li W. The 6 degrees-of-freedom range of motion of the L1-S1 vertebrae in young and middle-aged asymptomatic people. Front Surg. 2022;9:1002133. Open access (CC BY 4.0); checked against the full text on Europe PMC (PMC9643460).
laws.table: Table 1, young group (n = 14, 20-30 years), mean in vivo dual-fluoroscopic intervertebral rotation range about each motion's primary axis: flex = flexion-extension about the mediolateral axis (45 deg trunk flexion to maximal extension, so not the maximal flexion range); lateral = left-right bend about the anteroposterior axis; rotate = left-right torsion about the craniocaudal axis.
laws.assumptions: Repository assumptions, not published results: motion is shared across levels in proportion to each level's range (ratio = range_i / sum(range)); the young cohort's means are used and the large inter-subject SDs are not; level limits are the cited ranges scaled to the parity-standard total range of the driver coordinate, one factor per motion.
laws.source: Xu F, Zhou S, Li Z, Jiang S, Chen Z, Sun Z, Li W. Front Surg 9:1002133 (2022), Table 1, young group (n=14), per-level primary-axis rotation range; shares proportional to range (repository assumption)
